analyst_view.overall: Excelsior (13th, 14 points) host Telstar (16th, 10 points) on Saturday in a relegation six-pointer; Telstar coach Henk Brugge called these year-end games ones where points can and maybe must be won. Excelsior under Ruben den Uil ended a run of four defeats (including 0-9 at Twente) with a 3-2 win at Feyenoord on 21 November, their first league win in De Kuip since 1980, with on-loan winger Sliti outstanding. Telstar lost 1-3 at home to PEC Zwolle the same night after defensive errors. The numbers count Alders and Mendes as out for Telstar, but both came off the bench against PEC and are fit; Seedorf (hurt in a friendly against Antwerp) is the only Telstar player still listed as doubtful, and Excelsior have no injuries listed (Groen is back from a ban). Danny Makkelie referees, as the numbers already assume (he books about 2.5 per game); news for this match was thin, with no full preview found.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.4 goals and already add Telstar's 14 goals and Excelsior's 22 conceded in their last six. They also add about +6% to Excelsior's goals for Gerald Alders being out and take about 3.5% off Telstar's for Rui Mendes, but both came on as subs against PEC Zwolle on 21 November and are fit. Undoing that nets out to a hair lower, so I move it 1%, to about 3.37.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.7 corners and already trim Excelsior's share for their few corners lately (19 in six). Excelsior did score from a corner header (Widell) at Feyenoord, but I found nothing on tactics or line-ups that the numbers can't see, so I stay at about 9.7.

cards.text: The numbers say 2.4 cards and already take about 12% off for Danny Makkelie, who books about 2.5 per game, and a little off Telstar for fewer cards lately. This is a six-pointer near the bottom that Telstar's coach has called a must-take-points game, and the numbers carry no stakes adjustment for it, so I lean mildly higher, to about 2.5.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.3 shots and already move Excelsior down (-12.5%) and Telstar up (+9.9%) for recent form. Excelsior's win at Feyenoord shows some life in their attack, with Sliti in form, while Telstar were the better side on the ball against PEC by Brugge's account; with Mendes and Alders fit and only Seedorf doubtful these roughly balance, so I stay at about 26.3.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.9 shots on target and already count Excelsior's poor accuracy lately (12 on target in six) and Telstar's better run (37). Nothing new on either side's attack beyond Telstar's squad being nearly fully fit, which the form figures already reflect, so I stay at about 9.9.
